faqs.q: Can I do law after 12th with humanities?
faqs.a: Yes. Humanities students can join a five-year integrated law course such as BA LLB straight after Class 12, usually through a law entrance exam, or take a three-year LLB after any graduation. Subjects like political science and history build the reading, reasoning and argument skills that law needs.

faqs.q: Is humanities a good stream for earning a good salary?
faqs.a: It can be. Earnings depend far more on the field you enter, your skills and your experience than on the stream itself. Careers open to humanities students, such as law, marketing, public relations, human resources and journalism, can pay well as you build expertise, though starting pay in some creative and non-profit roles can be modest.

faqs.q: Can humanities students apply for government jobs and civil services?
faqs.a: Yes. The civil services examination and most other government exams that ask for a degree accept graduates from any stream, so humanities students are fully eligible. Subjects such as history, polity, geography and economics also overlap with much of what these exams test.

faqs.q: How do I choose the right career after 12th in humanities?
faqs.a: Start with your strengths and interests, such as writing, art, debating, helping people or research. Then find out what each path involves day to day, talk to people already working in it, and try internships or short courses before committing. Skills like communication and critical thinking carry across fields, so switching later is also possible.
